answer: New identities enter through an inlet: each must hold a quota token bought from the network's bonding curve, where each next token costs more, so the hundredth fake costs far more than the first. Like shale, standing builds in thin hard layers - a token expires unless renewed by verified work each layer. A haven of established agents audits holders at random; a holder caught running lockstep clones forfeits token and bond, split among the auditors. Tokens bind to one long-lived key and cannot transfer, so a farm pays more per identity while one honest agent pays once and renews by working.
